clue.text: Singing Billy. A short history of a religious man

parts.note: Billy Budd is the title role of Britten's opera, so he is a Billy who sings
hist. is the standard shortened form of the word history

explanation.surface: A biography of a singer called Billy, told briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: BILLY BUDD is Benjamin Britten's opera about a sailor, hence 'Singing Billy'; the full stop after it is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Buddha's teaching is a man of that faith.

clue.text: Note the steps in football

definitions.note: the thing found in a football, a noun

parts.note: B is a musical note
a ladder is a set of steps

explanation.surface: Remarking on the footwork of a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: Old leather footballs had an inflatable rubber bag inside, which is what 'in football' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The inflatable rubber bag inside a leather ball, named after the body's urine sac.

clue.text: Deadpan comic provokes R.A.F. hero to swearing

parts.note: dam is an old spelling of the oath damn
Buster Keaton was the great deadpan comedian of silent film

explanation.surface: A stone-faced comedian goads an airman into cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: Buster Keaton provokes the hero to swear 'Dam(n), Buster!', so the oath comes first; the 1943 raid on German dams made the squadron's airmen famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The airmen of 617 Squadron who breached the Ruhr dams in 1943 became celebrated RAF heroes.

clue.text: Seeking reduction he's healthier astride a child's horse

definitions.note: reads as 'he's seeking a reduction', describing a person

indicators.note: astride means the word for healthier sits with its legs either side of the other piece

parts.note: haler is the comparative of hale, healthy
gee-gee, GG, is nursery talk for a horse

explanation.surface: A fitter man sits on a rocking horse while bargaining down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astride' says the healthier man sits over the child's horse, as on a rocking horse; gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargainer argues over the price, trying to beat it down.

clue.text: As 1,003 were in Spain; by a notorious D.J.

definitions.text: As 1,003 were in Spain; by a notorious D.J.

parts.words: As 1,003 were in Spain; by a notorious D.J.
parts.note: Leporello's catalogue aria in Don Giovanni counts a thousand and three conquests in Spain; D.J. is Don Juan

explanation.surface: A tally of women in Spain credited to an infamous disc jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: D.J. reads as disc jockey but is Don Juan; in Mozart's Don Giovanni his servant lists 'in Spagna mille e tre', 1,003 in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan's conquests were women he had lured into bed.

clue.text: Indicating Y's presence is most unorthodox

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: the most unorthodox thing, the extreme of unorthodoxy

parts.note: saying 'here's' points something out, so it indicates
the presence of Y is simply the letter Y itself

explanation.surface: Pointing out that a Y is present counts as wildly unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'Here's Y!' and you have pointed to Y being present; run together it spells the word for belief furthest from orthodoxy.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is belief contrary to accepted doctrine, the extreme of departing from orthodoxy.

clue.text: Workmen fish with an implement

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farmhands
a pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Labourers go fishing with a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A handspike is a wooden bar used as a lever, for instance on a ship's capstan.

clue.text: Answers material fabrications

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
lies are fabrications, made-up stories

explanation.surface: Responses that are thoroughly made up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material fabrications' reads as substantial falsehoods, but material is a cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Replies are responses given to questions.

clue.text: Top-of-the-house hair style

definitions.meaning: a wooden roof tile laid in overlapping rows
a short bob, tapered at the nape, fashionable in the 1920s

explanation.surface: A haircut fit for the head of the household.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a thin wooden roofing tile and a short tapered women's haircut.

clue.text: All-time end of hostilities

parts.note: the last great battle, foretold for the end of time, after which there is no more fighting

explanation.surface: A ceasefire that lasts for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-time' reads as 'record-breaking', but means at the end of all time: the final battle of Revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Revelation this is the site of the final battle at the end of the world.

clue.text: He's too self-righteous to steal

definitions.meaning: old slang for steal or pilfer

explanation.surface: A man too sanctimonious to commit theft.
explanation.definitionFit: A prim moralist is a self-righteous person, and in old thieves' cant to prig was to pilfer.

clue.text: Dishonest way of making a score

definitions.meaning: betraying someone while seeming loyal, treacherous
two crosses, XX, make the Roman numeral twenty, a score

explanation.surface: A crooked method of getting a result.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, and XX, a pair of crosses, is twenty in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying a partner is treachery; and XX, two crosses, is the Roman numeral for twenty.

clue.text: Went to bed just about fagged out

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
fagged out is British slang for exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone so nearly worn out that they turned in for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just about fagged out' reads as nearly exhausted, but 'about' gives RE and 'fagged out' gives TIRED; 'just' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire for the night is to go off to sleep.

clue.text: The making of a Swiss confection, or of a solicitor?

definitions.text: The making of a Swiss confection
definitions.meaning: rolling up a sponge into a Swiss roll
a solicitor is admitted by being entered on the Roll of the profession

explanation.surface: Asks what makes a cake, or a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as en-ROL-ment, forming a roll; solicitors in England are admitted by being entered on the Roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entered on a register, the Roll, admits a solicitor; and rolling a sponge is 'en-rolling' it.

clue.text: Barrie's little man drops one in, church

indicators.note: drops means the letter for one is let fall out of the word

parts.note: J. M. Barrie wrote the novel and play The Little Minister
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The little man from Barrie's story pops into church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops one in' reads as dropping in on a visit, but the minister drops I (one); 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, such as York's cathedral.

clue.text: It's liable to be proved a false statement

indicators.note: false suggests the letters are not genuine as they stand and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that may turn out to be untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' rearranges STATEMENT. 'proved' reads as shown true, but a will is proved when probate confirms it; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will is proved, that is admitted to probate, before it takes effect.

clue.text: Set aside a loan to Antony

parts.note: 'lend me your ears', Mark Antony asks the crowd in Julius Caesar, so an ear is a loan
Antony's forename is Mark, as in Mark Antony

explanation.surface: A sum reserved to be lent to a man named Antony.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar Mark Antony says 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears': the ear lent is to (Mark) Antony.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to reserve them for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Movement of an Italian poet

parts.note: taken as written
Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A section from an Italian poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' reads as a political movement, but it is a piece of a symphony marked at walking pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow movement of a symphony or sonata is often named by its tempo marking.

clue.text: Like the feast in a hamper

definitions.text: Like the feast in a hamper

parts.words: Like the feast in a hamper
parts.note: a picnic packed in a basket can be carried anywhere, a feast that travels

explanation.surface: A picnic packed in a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: A movable feast is a church festival with no fixed date, such as Easter; here it is a meal in a basket that can be carried about.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed picnic is portable, a festival like Easter has no fixed date, and both senses fit.

clue.text: " In quiet she -- ; Ah! would that I did too " (Arnold)

definitions.text: In quiet she -- ; Ah! would that I did too

parts.words: In quiet she -- ; Ah! would that I did too
parts.note: a line from Matthew Arnold's poem Requiescat, with the missing verb for resting in peace

explanation.surface: A quotation from Arnold with its verb left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold's elegy Requiescat has 'In quiet she reposes: Ah! would that I did too'; the answer fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The dead woman of the poem rests at peace, lying still in quiet.

clue.text: As one might cordiality-having tried a double perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be differently arranged
double says the single letter a is written twice over

explanation.surface: Showing warmth after downing a double whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TRIED with AA, 'a' doubled. 'a double' looks like a stiff drink; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One radiates warmth or cordiality, giving it off in all directions.

clue.text: Publicity man's getting through, to get on nicely

parts.note: PRO, public relations officer, is a publicity man; with the 's it gives PROS
per means through or by way of, as in per post

explanation.surface: A press officer getting through his work and doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or do well.

clue.text: Showed signs of honest labour dishonestly exploited

definitions.meaning: of workers, overworked for poor pay

explanation.surface: Contrasts honest toil with exploitation of workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard work makes one perspire, and sweatshop labour is overworked and underpaid.

clue.text: He brings out the worst in the best of us

definitions.text: He brings out the worst in the best of us

parts.words: He brings out the worst in the best of us
parts.note: in a canonisation case one official argues against the candidate saint, raising every fault

explanation.surface: Someone who makes even good people behave badly.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a bad influence, but in the Catholic process of making saints one official must bring out any faults in the very best candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: The Church official who argues against a proposed saint's canonisation, and by extension anyone arguing the contrary side.

clue.text: At last a toffee-nosed type

definitions.meaning: an old word for a cobbler, who works at a shoemaker's last
toffee-nosed is British slang for stuck-up and condescending

explanation.surface: Finally, here is a stuck-up person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' reads as 'finally', but a last is the shoe-shaped block a cobbler works on, and an old word for a cobbler is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler works at the last, and in old usage was so called; it is also a person who looks down on social inferiors.

clue.text: Can have perm and set? Perhaps it's a bit steep

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged otherwise, a hint to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A hairdresser asks whether a perm and set can be had, at a steep price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges CAN, PERM and SET. 'a bit steep' looks like a comment on the hairdresser's price, but it describes a steep slope; 'have' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarpment is a long steep slope or cliff edging a plateau.

clue.text: To go back always turn right

indicators.note: turn tells us to turn the word for always round, reading it backwards

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Advice that to return you should always turn to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' turns only the word for always, which then comes before the abbreviation for right; the surface makes 'turn right' a road direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To revert is to return to an earlier state or habit.

clue.text: Indented for new retreads?

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Asks whether new remoulded tyres have notched treads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges RETREADS.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated edge is notched with teeth like a saw.
